results.title: One started + one terminal probe per use case (spec UIS-OBS-01)
results.desc: Workflow wrapper publishes started on entry and exactly one terminal on both success and failure paths
results.prose: Random spec draw (second hit on this standard — the shuffle is honest): standards/ui/domain-observability.spec.md, this time UIS-OBS-01 — every use-case invocation publishes one started probe and exactly one terminal probe. The gateway-operations wrapper enforces it structurally: a single run() helper publishes workflow.started + dependency.attempted on entry, and both the success and catch paths publish exactly one workflow.completed with the matching outcome (succeeded or failureOutcome(error)), all under a fresh correlationId/traceId per invocation. Because every use case funnels through this wrapper, per-case discipline can't drift — the spec's matrix requirement is satisfied by construction.
results.steps: Read gateway-operations.ts run wrapper; assert started-on-entry, terminal-on-success (succeeded), terminal-on-failure (failureOutcome), single wrapped path, correlation context.

results.title: Workspace-scoped isolation (upstream #4620 context)
results.desc: Sandbox in named workspace is listed only in that workspace
results.detail: first attempt: sandbox in un-created workspace vanished (create ok, ready=gone); retried WITH CreateWorkspace first: CreateWorkspace grpc=0, sandbox reached Ready in 25s, listed in its workspace, exec with workspace-scoped selector returns ws-exec-ok, cleanup clean
results.prose: Upstream #4620 adds --output to workspace create/get — workspace ergonomics investment — so I verified the isolation contract beneath it. First lesson: workspaces are NOT auto-created on first sandbox reference; a sandbox created in a nonexistent workspace is accepted then silently vanishes (create grpc=0, then gone). Explicit CreateWorkspace first fixes everything: the sandbox reached Ready in 25s, is listed only in its workspace, exec with a workspace-scoped selector works, and workspace+sandbox delete cleanly. That silent-vanish on an un-created workspace is a real UX trap worth knowing — the CLI's workspace create path exists precisely so users don't hit it.
steps: Attempt CreateSandbox in nonexistent workspace (accepted then vanished — trap documented)
CreateSandbox in the workspace; poll GetSandbox workspace-scoped until Ready
ExecSandbox with workspace selector — output returns
